keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Chutu row. The page gives no area: only a map caption "Location of the Chutus in South India". The Banavasi core is the researcher's radius; Konkan and Goa ("probably also gained control of the Konkan", places in Goa, as subordinates of the Bhojas) and the Anantapur-Srisailam coin finds are named on the page and not drawn. Until the Satavahana decline (c. 225) the Chutus were their feudatories and Cliopatria draws their land as Satavahana (102 of 228 cells).

region.text: Banavasi in Uttara Kannada and its country: "northern Karnataka" (the Satavahana page's south-western kingdom of the Chutus of Banavasi)

ledger.note: c. 125: Chutu rule begins at Banavasi. The page: "c. 125 CE: Chutu rule at Banavasi begins" (Michael Mitchiner speculates they were Shaka chiefs who became Satavahana feudatories after Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated Nahapana around 125 CE); infobox "1st century BCE" as established and "3rd century CE" as disestablished. The land is the researcher's reading of Banavasi.

ledger.note: c. 345: the Kadambas occupy Banavasi. "c. 345 CE: The Kadambas occupy Banavasi, which ends Chutu rule there." The page also says the line "came to an end probably in the first or second half of the third century, that is, around 250-275 CE", which contradicts its own c. 345.

region.text: Banavasi in Uttara Kannada and its country: "northern Karnataka" (the Satavahana page's south-western kingdom of the Chutus of Banavasi)

ledger.note: c. 345: Chutu rule ends at Banavasi under the Kadambas. Four Chutu inscriptions are dated within the 260s-340s, and an Abhira inscription from Nagarjunakonda of 278 attests King Sivalananda, which supports a life beyond 275.

wars.note: The page gives the year and the place and no battle; the Kadamba page (not opened here) has Mayurasharma founding the kingdom c. 345.

certainty.note: No border is given for any year; the extent is Banavasi and its country, with coin finds at Anantapur and southern Telangana and subordinate places in Goa not drawn.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks (sa-02-b asks for it). Two pages opened (budget 2-5): Chutu dynasty and Satavahana dynasty, which gives the split of the empire (the Chutus of Banavasi rule the south-west) but not its own date. Start 125 is the page's "Chutu rule at Banavasi begins" (a feudatory of the Satavahanas until their decline c. 225): the sa-02-b gap-filler should add a vassal_start (c. 125) and vassal_end (c. 225) to satavahana-dynasty, counterpart chutu-dynasty; Cliopatria draws the land as Satavahana until 223. End 345: the page gives both c. 345 (Kadamba occupation) and 250-275; 345 is the one with a dated event. The Kadamba dossier should list chutu-dynasty as predecessor for the Banavasi core in 345. Not drawn: the Konkan and Goa subordinates, Anantapur and southern Telangana coin finds, the Abhira-linked Sivalananda inscription. No ruler strip: the page gives regnal years only for single inscriptions. Gazetteer names needed: Banavasi (used as a coordinate radius).
